data.Documented value: Correlation of Local Unemployment Rates and North Carolina Community College Enrollments

The effect of business cycles, as evidenced by local unemployment rates, on individual community colleges needs to be understood so that public resources can be used to strategically align the supply and demand of educational opportunities. A countercyclical relationship indicates the ability to serve citizens may be most restricted during economic downturns when demand is highest. A quantitative Pearson product-moment correlation design was used in this study to determine the magnitude and strength of the relationship of local unemployment rates and enrollments from 1990 through 2016 in North Carolina’s 58 community colleges. Total full-time enrollment in three main categories of instruction was examined. There was a very weak negative correlation between local unemployment rates and total full-time equivalent enrollments, curriculum full-time equivalent enrollments, and continuing education full-time equivalent enrollments using aggregated data. There was no statistically significant correlation between local unemployment rates and basic skills full-time equivalent enrollments using aggregated data. Disaggregated data at the individual college level produced mixed results. Four colleges were significantly correlated in every category. Ten colleges were significantly correlated in three categories. Eight colleges were significantly correlated in two categories. Nineteen colleges were significantly correlated in one category. Seventeen colleges were not significantly correlated in any categories.

sections.heading: F&M Bank’s Nick Means expands financial empowerment efforts across Rowan
paragraphs: Rowan-Cabarrus Community College is set to play a pivotal role in facilitating financial empowerment initiatives across the Rowan County community. Nick Means, a community banking officer, has been instrumental in expanding these efforts. Through his leadership and educational initiatives, Means has been able to build trust, access, and opportunities for financial literacy and economic growth within the region. [[S2|Salisbury Post]] Means' approach is rooted in the belief that education is the key to unlocking financial empowerment.

He has been actively engaged in workshops, seminars, and one-on-one consultations to help community members understand the basics of banking, budgeting, and managing their finances. His methods have been highly effective, as evidenced by the positive feedback from participants. [[S2|Salisbury Post]] One of the significant outcomes of Means' efforts has been the establishment of a financial literacy program that has reached thousands of residents. This program, which includes interactive sessions, online resources, and community events, has been designed to make financial concepts accessible and engaging.

The program's success is evident in the increased participation rates and the reported improvements in financial knowledge and confidence among participants. [[S2|Salisbury Post]] Means' initiatives have also extended to small business owners, providing them with the tools and knowledge to manage their finances effectively. This has led to a noticeable increase in the number of small businesses that are able to secure loans and access credit, thereby boosting the local economy. The program's success has been recognized by local businesses, who have expressed their gratitude for the additional support and resources available to them.

[[S2|Salisbury Post]] The financial empowerment efforts of Nick Means have not been limited to Rowan County alone. His work has been recognized by the Rowan County Board of Commissioners, who have expressed their appreciation for the community's investment in financial education and empowerment. This recognition underscores the broader impact of Means' initiatives and the potential for similar programs to be replicated in other communities. [[S2|Salisbury Post]] While the success of Means' efforts is evident, it is important to acknowledge the challenges that come with expanding financial empowerment initiatives.

The lack of access to financial resources and information in some communities can make it difficult for individuals to participate in these programs. However, Means' approach has been designed to address these challenges by providing resources and support to those who may not have access to traditional financial education. sections.heading: Rowan Digital Infrastructure
paragraphs: ### Rowan-Cabarrus Community College to Facilitate Rowan Digital Infrastructure [[S4|Bing web evidence]] Rowan-Cabarrus Community College is set to lead the way in the development of Rowan Digital Infrastructure, a project designed to enhance the college's digital capabilities and infrastructure. This initiative is part of a broader effort to ensure that the college remains at the forefront of technological advancements and can better serve its students and the community it serves. [[S4|Bing web evidence]] The project, known as Rowan Digital Infrastructure, is a collaboration between Rowan-Cabarrus and other local and regional organizations. It aims to provide a robust and scalable digital infrastructure that can support the college's growing needs.

The project will involve the development of a hyperscale data center, which is a facility designed to provide high-speed internet access and storage capacity. This data center will be built to meet the highest standards of power and environmental efficiency, ensuring that it can support the college's operations and future growth. [[S4|Bing web evidence]] The hyperscale data center will be designed to deliver powered, permitted, and build-to-suit hyperscale capacity with unparalleled speed, customer alignment, and community trust. This means that the college will be able to provide reliable and fast internet access to its students and the community, while also ensuring that the data center is built and operated in a way that is responsible and sustainable.

[[S4|Bing web evidence]] The project is part of a larger effort to address the growing demand for skilled workers in technical and advanced manufacturing jobs. While data forecast that America will face a shortage of skilled workers in these areas within the next 10 years, enrollment in high school and college career and technical education pathways is down. Many of these jobs offer wages and benefits that equal or rival those of jobs requiring advanced degrees. If the demand for skilled workers exists, why is the supply of qualified applicants dwindling?

High schools and community colleges offer coursework and hands-on training in these areas. Can these two systems work together to encourage students to enter career and technical education pathways? [[S4|Bing web evidence]] This disquisition addresses the history of the declining enrollment in these programs, the intersystems cooperation that must happen to matriculate students from high school to college Associate in Applied Science programs, and one intervention that attempted to cross systemic barriers to connect high school staff and community college career and technical education programs.

sections.heading: Creating shared vision and facilitating transformation in community colleges
paragraphs: Rowan-Cabarrus Community College, situated in the Piedmont region of North Carolina, is embarking on a transformative journey to enhance its community engagement and strategic planning. This initiative, facilitated by the college's leadership, is designed to create a shared vision and facilitate a transformational change that aligns with the institution's goals and the aspirations of its community. [[S6|IRL University of Missouri St Louis]] The college's approach to this process is informed by the findings of a qualitative study conducted by the University of Missouri–St. Louis.

This research, "Creating shared vision and facilitating transformation in community colleges," identifies the key elements that contribute to the successful strategic planning of community colleges. The study suggests that the strategic planning process should involve the active participation of all stakeholders, including students, faculty, staff, and community members. The research also highlights the importance of leadership, cultural characteristics, and individual contributions in fostering a shared vision. [[S6|IRL University of Missouri St Louis]] To implement these best practices, Rowan-Cabarrus Community College has established a focus group process.

The college has conducted four homogeneous focus groups at each college, including leadership, students, faculty, and staff. The focus groups were designed to explore the role of leadership in the strategic planning process, the cultural characteristics of the college that influence the planning processes, and the role that each individual plays in the process. The research found that a combination of factors work in concert to enable the community colleges in the study to foster a shared vision. Attributes such as loyalty, servant leadership, communication, trust, and accountability are but a few of the necessary attributes found among the colleges in the research.

[[S6|IRL University of Missouri St Louis]] The college's approach to this process is also informed by the findings of a master's project conducted by the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. This project, "An Evaluation of The North Carolina Community College System's Pre-Homeownership Counseling Program," proposes primarily to address the use of the North Carolina Community College System's Pre-Homeownership Education Program. The evaluation is a first step at gathering information on the program's history, assessing current underutilization, and proposing recommendations and considerations for the program's future. The college hopes to share the contents of this project in a presentation to key leadership in the state's Community College System and housing counseling and homebuyer education network.

sections.heading: Reversing the enrollment decline in career and technical education career
paragraphs: Rowan-Cabarrus Community College is poised to play a pivotal role in reversing the downward trend of enrollment in career and technical education programs. The data from the University of North Carolina at Greensboro indicates that America is facing a significant shortage of skilled workers in technical and advanced manufacturing jobs within the next decade. This forecast underscores the urgency of the situation, as many of these jobs offer wages and benefits that rival those of jobs requiring advanced degrees. [[S7|NC Digital Online Collection of Knowledge]] The decline in enrollment in career and technical education programs is not just a statistic; it reflects a broader societal concern.

High schools and community colleges traditionally offer coursework and hands-on training in these areas, providing students with the foundational skills needed to enter the workforce. However, the traditional educational system has struggled to attract and retain students interested in these programs. This is where Rowan-Cabarrus Community College steps in, aiming to bridge the gap between high school and college career and technical education programs. [[S7|NC Digital Online Collection of Knowledge]] The intervention being implemented by Rowan-Cabarrus Community College is designed to facilitate the matriculation of students from high school to college Associate in Applied Science programs.

This initiative involves the collaboration between high school staff and community college career and technical education programs. By working together, these two systems can create a more seamless transition for students, ensuring that they are better prepared for the workforce upon graduation. [[S7|NC Digital Online Collection of Knowledge]] The success of this intervention is being evaluated through various metrics. The study conducted by East Tennessee State University, titled "The Attributes, Teaching Effectiveness, and Educational Commitment of Part-time Faculty in North Carolina Community Colleges," provides valuable insights into the attributes, teaching effectiveness, and educational commitment of part-time faculty.

The study found that part-time faculty were perceived as effective when compared to their full-time counterpart on the dimensions of Faculty/Student Interaction. This suggests that part-time faculty can contribute significantly to the educational experience, even if they are not full-time instructors. [[S7|NC Digital Online Collection of Knowledge]] However, the study also highlighted that full-time faculty were perceived more effective on Overall Quality of the Course, Lectures, Textbooks, and Reading Assignments. This indicates that while part-time faculty can be effective, they may not be as effective in certain areas as their full-time counterparts.

sections.heading: N.C. community college/industry interactions
paragraphs: ### Rowan-Cabarrus Community College to Facilitate N.C. Community College/Industry Interactions [[S1|NC Digital Online Collection of Knowledge]] Rowan-Cabarrus Community College is set to play a pivotal role in enhancing the collaborative efforts between community colleges and the private sector in North Carolina. This initiative is part of a broader effort to strengthen the relationship between educational institutions and local businesses, aiming to foster economic growth and workforce development. [[S1|NC Digital Online Collection of Knowledge]] The study conducted by the University of North Carolina at Greensboro, titled "N.C.

community college/industry interactions: Present status and future possibilities," provides a comprehensive overview of the current landscape of college-industry relationships in North Carolina community colleges. The research involved surveys sent to academic deans across fifty-eight institutions and interviews with six community college administrators who are responsible for managing college-industry relationships. The findings reveal that while there is a growing recognition of the importance of industry partnerships, there is still much to be done to fully leverage these relationships for economic benefit. [[S1|NC Digital Online Collection of Knowledge]] The conceptual framework for managing college-industry programs includes both strategic and operational planning components.

The strategic planning component focuses on long-term goals and objectives, while the operational planning component deals with day-to-day activities and service delivery. Both components are based on a sequence of planning, selecting, organizing, and delivering services, followed by evaluation. This framework aims to provide a structured approach to managing college-industry programs, ensuring that they are effective and efficient. [[S1|NC Digital Online Collection of Knowledge]] In addition to the conceptual framework, the study also highlights the importance of linking community colleges' services to economic development.

This linkage is crucial for ensuring that the educational programs offered by community colleges are directly relevant to the needs of the local economy. By doing so, the college can better prepare students for the workforce and contribute to the growth of the local economy. [[S1|NC Digital Online Collection of Knowledge]] The initiative by Rowan-Cabarrus Community College is part of a larger effort to enhance the collaboration between educational institutions and the private sector. This collaboration is essential for creating a more competitive and innovative economy, and for providing students with the skills and knowledge necessary to succeed in the job market.
